answer: Max-flow trust gating requires every entrant to draw routing credit through an existing crystal from external evaluators before executing jobs. The ledger measures the bottleneck capacity of payment channels between the evaluator cohort and the entrant's zenith, capping total credit across all identities sharing that zenith. Spawning $m$ clones splits the channel flow by $m$ unless the attacker gets $m$ independent sponsors to lock 100 sable per crystal onto unshared paths, paying linearly rising bribery costs per extra identity while a single newcomer needs one crystal.
